title: Dual-Format Heading Extraction for HTML & Markdown Reports
description:
This tour walks through the changes made to support HTML-format library reports in the helix-cli. Previously, the `hlx library show` command only extracted headings using a Markdown regex (`/^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/`), which fails on HTML reports (`

Title

`). The fix adds an HTML heading regex tried first, with the original Markdown regex preserved as a fallback — ensuring backward compatibility with existing Markdown reports. A `filePath` field was also added to the local type to support optional format detection. Zero new runtime dependencies were introduced.

steps.description: This is the only file that needed changes for HTML report support. The comment commands (`comments-list.ts`, `comments-post.ts`) are format-agnostic — they operate on anchor strings passed via `--section` and never parse report content. All format-dependent heading extraction lives here in `show.ts`. The goal: try an HTML heading regex first, fall back to the existing Markdown regex, and produce identical output in both cases.
steps.title: Overview: The Only Format-Dependent File

steps.description: The `filePath` field is added as optional (`filePath?: string | null`) to the local `LibraryItemDetail` type. This mirrors the new field added to the server (helix-global-server) API response, which now includes `filePath` for each library item. The field is optional and backward-compatible — existing Markdown report responses without `filePath` continue to work. While `filePath` could be used for format detection, the primary detection method is content inspection via the HTML regex (see next steps).
steps.title: Step L1: Add filePath to Local Type

steps.description: This is the core change. The regex `/<h([1-6])(?:\s+[^>]*?id="([^"]*)"[^>]*)?>(.+?)<\/h\1>/i` is checked first for each line of report content. It extracts: (1) heading level 1-6 from the tag name, (2) the `id` attribute when present — used directly as the anchor slug to avoid any slugify discrepancy, and (3) the raw heading text with nested HTML tags stripped via `replace(/<[^>]+>/g, '')` for clean display. This regex assumes headings appear on a single line, which matches the format generated by the updated agent prompts.
steps.title: Step L2a: HTML Heading Regex (Primary Pattern)

steps.description: After a successful HTML heading match, a `continue` statement skips the rest of the loop body for that line. This prevents the same line from also being tested against the Markdown heading regex below. Without this guard, an HTML heading line could theoretically match both patterns and be processed twice. The `continue` makes the HTML path and Markdown path mutually exclusive per line.
steps.title: Step L2b: `continue` Prevents Double-Processing

steps.description: The original Markdown heading regex `/^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/` is completely unchanged. It only executes for lines that did NOT match the HTML pattern above (due to the `continue`). This ensures full backward compatibility: any existing Markdown report is processed exactly as before. Both the HTML and Markdown paths produce output in the same format — heading level indicators with slug annotations and comment counts — so the rest of the display logic is shared and unchanged.
steps.title: Step L2c: Markdown Heading Regex (Preserved Fallback)

steps.description: The implementation is complete and minimal. Only `show.ts` was modified. The HTML regex is tried first; the original Markdown regex is the fallback. The `filePath` type addition is optional and non-breaking. TypeScript compilation passes with zero errors (`npx tsc --noEmit`). No runtime dependencies were added — the CLI retains its zero-dependency design. All comment annotation paths (`comments-list.ts`, `comments-post.ts`) are untouched and remain format-agnostic. The single deferred risk is multi-line HTML headings, which are not generated by the current agent prompts and can be addressed if needed in a future iteration.
steps.title: Summary: Clean Code Paths, Zero New Dependencies
